html:
Faisal was the king of Saudi Arabia from 1964 to 1975, a son of Ibn Saud who had served as foreign minister since the 1930s.

As crown prince and prime minister he pushed reforms past the religious scholars: state schools for girls in 1960, the abolition of slavery in 1962 (Saudi Arabia abolishes slavery), and television in 1965. He took power from his spendthrift brother King Saud in 1964. He backed Islamic unity against the Arab nationalism of Egypt's Nasser.

In 1973 he led the Arab oil embargo against the United States and other backers of Israel, which made oil prices jump fourfold. In March 1975 he was shot dead by a nephew in Riyadh. See also Saudi Arabia.
sum: Faisal was the king of Saudi Arabia from 1964 to 1975, a son of Ibn Saud who had served as foreign minister since the 1930s.
